name: Tesamorelin

lead: Tesamorelin (Egrifta) is a synthetic analogue of growth hormone-releasing hormone approved in the United States to reduce excess abdominal fat in adults with HIV-associated lipodystrophy. It is injected daily.

It is sometimes discussed in body-composition and peptide circles for visceral fat reduction. Its approval and evidence cover only that specific patient group, and it cannot remove fat from the cheeks or jawline selectively.

paras: Tesamorelin stimulates the pituitary to release endogenous growth hormone in a pulsatile fashion, which raises IGF-1. Growth hormone promotes lipolysis, with a particular effect on visceral adipose tissue, which explains the reduction in trunk fat in trials.

Reported effects include joint pain, fluid retention, injection-site reactions and glucose intolerance, and raised IGF-1 prompts caution about malignancy. It is prescription-only and expensive, fat returns after stopping, and benefits in people without HIV lipodystrophy are not established.
